ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The expression denotes go wash your bowl in these Chan records. Its wording is go wash your bowl.
EvidenceBody: It is Zhaozhou Congshen's closing reply when a newcomer requests instruction, says that he has eaten his gruel, and is told to wash the bowl; the record reports that the newcomer awakened. Zhaozhou's own record also uses the gruel question and exact command after a question about the student's own self. Later masters reopen the line. Dahui Zonggao says that many places raised and annotated it, restates washing the bowl without the final imperative, and asks whether instruction was given. Foyan Qingyuan says he ate gruel and washed his bowl that morning but did not awaken, then asks why. Wuwei Zongtai answers an entering interview with the exact command and is told that he knows the road's affair but not its flavor. Baohua Xian calls the exact command drawing legs on a snake. An ordinary cleanup command thereby becomes a stable, attributable public-case line repeatedly quoted, reenacted, and challenged.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: For 洗鉢盂去, the stored cases establish this term-specific deployment: Literally, go wash your bowl.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: One imperative and one corpus-wide case sense. Different appraisals do not make different things. Component-only washing evidence is labelled family and does not count. Distinguish the full command from wash the bowl (洗鉢盂), the gruel question, and bowl (鉢盂).
DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Aliases retrieve the same attested referent as go wash your bowl in ordinary English.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: All selected cases retain go wash your bowl despite different predicates.
